newsitem.title: USA: GCA July coffee stock data seen neutral to bearish.
newsitem.headline: GCA July coffee stock data seen neutral to bearish.

text.p: New York coffee futures may come under some pressure after monthly inventory data released late Friday showed an increase in U.S. consumer coffee stocks, traders and analysts said.
Supplies of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses rose in July by 219,000 60-kg bags, to 2,335,000 bags, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported.
"I view it as rather negative," said PaineWebber analyst Bernard Savaiko. "It is bearish at a time when people are talking about tightness and may be indicative of weak consumption."
Other analysts said, however, that the market's reaction may be muted given its recent weak tone in anticipation of a GCA stock build.

Most industry sources expected the data to show an increase in U.S. green coffee inventories of some 150,000 60-kg bags during July, although some dealers predicted a stock build of up to 250,000 bags.
"It is neutral to somewhat negative" said Dean Witter analyst Corey Bell. "The market anticipated some build, but given the technical picture the build is a bit negative."
On Friday, CSCE spot September fell 6.60 cents, to three-week low of 177.95 cents.

Some market participants speculated that the increase in U.S. inventories may come from coffee unsuitable for exchange certification and therefore may not have much of an impact on the New York market.

They noted the ports of New York and New Orleans, where the CSCE has warehouses, posted the largest gain in coffee stocks. New York stocks rose by 130,000 bags to 461,000 bags, the GCA said. Inventories increased by 88,000 bags, to 1,005,000 bags in New Orleans.
"New York and New Orleans rose which makes me wonder why the coffee didn't move into certified stocks," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes.
"If it were good quality and came in the month of July they could have been used against the July contract. Or is someone holding it off until September?"

Concerns there may be a shortage of exchange-certified coffee for delivery against the September contract drove the spot contract to a two-month high of 209.75 cents last week and stretched the September/December switch to more than 30 cents.
But talk that the price surge would attract some coffee to the board, an absence of roaster participation and no major drawdown in CSCE certified coffee stocks have combined to ease supply concerns.

After Friday's close, the CSCE reported exchange-certified coffee stocks in the U.S. warehouses fell by 149 60-kg bags as of August 14, to 91,971 bags. An additional 7,500 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
